text: Boss! Welcome to headquarters. It's not much yet: a desk, a map, a kettle. But it's yours, and I've got a feeling about you.
The desk on the left is what needs you right now. The map shows who leads where. Everything else is in the files along the top.
The whole country argues about something every month. Open Debates, pick a side, and say it your way. People remember how you said it.
You get three moves a month. Speak, start your own argument, open an office somewhere, dig into the competition. No wrong answers, boss. Well. Mostly.
When you're ready, press play and the weeks roll on. I'll be right here. I'm always right here.
New month, boss. Three fresh moves. The country's waiting.
A new month! I've cleared your diary. Well, I've cleared it of things I didn't think you'd enjoy.
Morning, boss. Coffee's on the desk, and so are the debates.
Another month. You know, I keep a list of everything you get right. I need a bigger notebook.
Three moves this month. Make them count. Not that you'd do anything else.
Fresh month, fresh headlines. Somebody out there is saying something you could answer.

A dip before the jump. Every great comeback starts with one.
Steady. Solid. A foundation, boss. You can build a palace on a foundation.
Holding firm while everyone else wobbles. That's leadership.
No change this month. The calm before something, I'd say.

The annual numbers, boss. A year of your work, all on one sheet of paper.

The quarterly ledger. I've sharpened your pencils.
Money in, money out. You always know where it does the most good.
A few donors have been in touch. Generous people. Very generous. I'm sure it's because they believe in you.
It's everywhere! My cousin sent it to me. My cousin doesn't even like politics!

Did you see that? Of course you did. You were there. You were magnificent.
That's the one they'll play at your retirement party. Decades from now, obviously.
I think you made a great point, boss.
Bold. Very bold. The country isn't ready for that kind of honesty yet. They will be.
The commentators didn't get it. Commentators never get it.
Let's call that a conversation starter.
That's telling them, boss.
Lovely. I'd have said it the same way. Well, not as well.
That one's going on the wall.
They'll be quoting that in the cafés tonight.
Short, clear, unmistakably you.

The papers buried it. Their loss. Literally, their readers' loss.
Not everyone's ready to hear the truth on a Tuesday.
This one's big, boss. The whole country's arguing. Whatever you say gets quoted.
Everyone's talking about it. If you're going to say something, now's the time. If you're not, that's a statement too.
A new office! I've ordered a sign. A big one.
Volunteers, a noticeboard and a kettle. That's how empires start, boss.
The locals love it. Well, the ones who came. They brought cake.
A new direction. Visionary. Some of our people will grumble, but they always come round. Mostly.
Changing course takes courage. Lucky we have plenty.
Between us, boss, they were holding you back.
One door closes. Frankly, it was a draughty door.
They'll regret it. People always do, once you've won.
Generous people, those donors. And so discreet.
Money's money, boss. It doesn't come with opinions. Usually.
Tonight's the big debate. Lights, cameras, and you. They don't stand a chance.
The final debate, boss. Just be yourself. Your self is very electable.
Three months to the election. I've stopped sleeping. You should keep sleeping; one of us needs to look fresh.
The home stretch, boss. Every move counts double now. Well, it feels that way.
We did it! You did it! I always said so. I have it in writing!
The largest party in the Assembly. I'd like to say I'm surprised, boss, but I'm not.
The country wasn't ready for you, boss. Not yet.
A moral victory. The best kind. The other kind is overrated.
Tip, boss: a story already in the headlines is far easier to turn into a national argument.
Speak for the sides that are yours. Heat on someone else's issue warms someone else's voters.
Offices take a while to pay off, but they never stop working. Like me.
Provocative lines catch fire. Sometimes the fire is on us. Mostly it's on them.
Say the same kind of thing often enough and people start to recognise your voice. That's charisma, boss.
Staying out of a fight is allowed. Nobody can quote what you didn't say.
Business money is easy money. Just don't let anyone see the receipt.

Your causes are your brand. Two is the limit; pick the ones with the most angry voters.
Whatever happens next, it was an honour, boss. Really.

Unemployment crisis
Rising prices make the economy and public services matter more, cost the government support and push up unrest.
Rising slowly

Answer the letters
You answered the letters until midnight. Nobody will notice, except the people who wrote them.
Thank the volunteers
You went round the phone bank with a box of pastries. Two volunteers cried. One asked for a selfie.
Call the local editor
You rang the editor of the paper back home, just to talk. It will be a friendlier headline next week, or it won't.
Sign the posters
You signed four hundred posters for the branch in {home}. Your hand will forgive you by Thursday.
Go to a wedding
A volunteer's daughter got married and you went. You danced badly, which went down well.
Read the comments
You read the comments under your last speech. Carlos told you not to. Carlos was right.
Too few speeches yet for people to know how you sound.
No one voice stands out: people aren't sure who you are yet.
Folksy and often over the line: entertaining, never boring, rarely taken at your word.
Fiery, and often over the line: you start fights and people come to watch.
Hopeful, with an edge: a better country, and harsh words for whoever stands in its way.
Mostly hopeful: you talk about the country it could be.
Mostly measured: calm, careful, in charge.

Calm, serious, in charge. Older and middle-class voters trust it; the young and the fed-up find it dull.

Angry on their behalf. Working people and the fed-up love it; the comfortable flinch.

The clip of you saying it is on every channel.

Plain talk and a joke, like at the kitchen table. The young and the provinces warm to it; the well-off wince.
It came across as down to earth.
The line has become a catchphrase.
The joke fell flat, and people noticed.
A picture of a better country, from someone outside the usual game. The young and the middle class lean in; the fed-up and the old roll their eyes.
It sounded like a better country. Some believed it.
The line is everywhere: people are quoting it to each other.
A promise that big made people laugh, and not with you.
The edge on a style: said to start a fight. It gets noticed and taken seriously, and it blows up more often.
Outrage on every channel.
The most shared clip of the month. Love it or hate it, everyone saw it.
Even people who agree with you are wincing.
Champion an issue

Campaign hard on one of your manifesto's issues to win its single-issue voters: people who care about that issue above everything else. You can campaign on two issues at a time. Claims are cheapest while nobody is talking about the issue; when it later dominates the news, many more voters become single-issue voters and its owner gains most.
Grassroots organising
Door-to-door work and local branches in one region. Turns supporters into core voters and gets them to the polls. Slow, but it lasts.
Opposition research

Pay investigators to dig into a rival. You may find something you can release later. You may also get caught. Friendly journalists at an honest outlet dig better and are caught less, and a story they run hits harder.
Release a dossier
Leak what you found to the press. It weakens the rival's support and stability, and lowers trust in politics, which helps outsiders like you.
Win over a branch

Only possible when a rival is unstable, and once every six months per party. One of their local branches crosses over to you: its organisers and some of its loyal voters, who bring their views with them. Very occasionally one of their politicians comes too.
Provoke outrage
Say something deliberately shocking to get your party's name everywhere. Recognition jumps and anti-system voters cheer, but the middle class is appalled and business donors back away.

The shops are gouging you and the government is watching. Price controls now!
My neighbour counts coins at the bakery now. She never used to count coins.
Somebody is getting rich off your empty fridge. I'll give you their names.
Imagine a week when the shopping costs what it cost the week before. That isn't a miracle. It's a decision.
We will establish a cross-party commission to examine the drivers of price formation.

Every pezo the state prints is a pezo stolen from your shopping bag!
You don't fix a leaky roof by painting the ceiling. Stop the money printing.
If you want queues for bread, ask the people who want price controls. They've done it before.
Picture a high street with three bakeries fighting over your custom. That's how prices fall, and it's closer than you think.

Erland has had bad years before. With a little help, next year's harvest will be the best in a decade.

Farming is a business. Some businesses fail.

A loaf is a loaf. My kids can't tell where the wheat came from.

Join the farmers' rain-day supper in a village square
I'll stand with these farmers in the sun, and in the rain when it comes.

Some people in the capital laugh at Harvest Day. Let them. Erland knows better.

Join the picket line
Forty thousand people cannot live on promises. Pay them!
I brought tea for the night shift. The owners brought lawyers.

A fair wage and a factory that lasts. We can have both.
Side with the factory owners

Strikes are a luxury for people who've never had to make a payroll.
My father ran a workshop with six men. A month like this would have closed him.
Call for state arbitration
Put both sides in a room with an independent arbitrator, and don't let them out until it's done.
Nobody wins a strike. Get them round a table, and bring biscuits.
The government is hiding under its desk. Arbitration, now!
Every strike ends at a table. Let's get there before anyone loses a month's pay.

foreign agitators

Ask who funds the strike committee. I hear they speak Dillihani.

Stay out of it

Golba's Founders Weekend outsells Harvest Day
Shops across {country} decked themselves out for Golba's Founders Weekend this year: flags, fireworks, forty percent off. The Harvest Day markets in Erland report their quietest year on record.
Defend Harvest Day: buy local this year
Every country borrows customs. Ours deserve not to be crowded out by a sale.
We're giving away our own holidays for forty percent off a television!
Golba can keep its fireworks. Our markets have plum cake and a brass band.
Let's make Harvest Day so good the Golbans start copying us.
If you need a Golban holiday to feel festive, Golba is a short flight.
Say people can celebrate what they like
Culture isn't protected by telling people where to shop.
My kids like both. They also like two dinners.
A confident country isn't afraid of a few fireworks.
Harvest Day lost to a sale. Maybe ask why, before blaming the sale.
Propose a tax on foreign holiday advertising
Foreign chains spend millions selling us their calendar. Let them pay for the privilege.
If Golba wants to throw a party here, it can pay for the hall.
The Language Academy wants Golban words out of adverts
A study finds one in three {national} teenagers mixes Golban words into almost every sentence. The Language Academy asks for a ban on Golban words in advertising and on shop signs.
Back the ban
Our language carried us through four hundred years. It can carry an advert.
My grandson told me his breakfast was "next level". It was toast.
Let's give our children a language rich enough that they don't need to borrow.
If you can't sell a sofa in {national}, it's probably a bad sofa.

Bans don't make a culture. Money for our own artists does.
If you want kids to sing in {national}, give them something good to sing.
The next song every teenager hums could be ours. Let's pay for it to be made.
Norbanian food takes over {city}'s old market

Celebrate it: the market has never been busier
A busy market is a living market. New stalls bring customers for everyone.
The queue was forty minutes. That's a market doing well.
This is what Yamlin always was: a port where the whole world comes for lunch.

Protect the old traders with a rent cap
Keep the market open to everyone, and affordable for the families who built it.
Three generations of the same butcher. That's worth a rent cap.
Speculators are buying the stalls and blaming the noodles!
A market where the butcher and the noodle stall both make a living. That's the whole point of a market.
Say the market is losing its {national} character
Walk through {city}'s market and tell me which country you're in!
I went for a sausage and came back with chopsticks.
A market should look like the town it serves.
Petrol passes ten pezos a litre

The NUP says fuel prices are set on world markets and there is little it can do.
Demand a cut in fuel tax
Tax is a third of the price. Cut it for a year and let people get to work.
The Treasury makes a fortune every time you fill up. Give it back!
Nobody drives to work for fun. Stop taxing people for having a job.
Let's be the country where you get to work without counting litres.
Cap fuel prices by law
A temporary cap, paid for by a tax on the companies making record profits from this.
Ten pezos a litre while the oil companies count their money? Cap it!
My cousin drives a delivery van. This week he paid to go to work.
A litre you can afford every week, whatever happens in the world.

The cheapest litre of petrol is the one you never need. That means trains and buses that work.
Picture a Cranebo where the bus is faster than the car. That's the way out of this.
If you live in the city and drive to work, the price is a hint.
Village bakeries in {province} close as flour doubles

A small subsidy keeps a village alive. It costs less than the van.
A village without a bakery is a village waiting to empty.
Fresh bread in every village in the morning. That's not much to ask of a country.

Publish the grain stocks, warehouse by warehouse. Speculation doesn't survive daylight.
Somebody is sitting on the grain while your bakery closes!
Find out who's storing the wheat. I'd start with whoever just bought a boat.

Prices rise, then supply follows. Interfering now only makes the next shortage worse.
People buy bread at the supermarket now. The village bakery is a lovely memory.
High prices bring new bakers. In five years Fauran will have better bread than ever.

Four thousand families with a future in {city}. I'll take that deal.

We are not paying a foreign billionaire to take our land!
If you have to pay a guest to stay, he isn't a guest.

Leaked list: two thousand {nationals} with secret accounts in James

2.5 billion for a stadium in Cranebo

Half the world will be watching Cranebo. We can't play in a car park.

National team striker stays silent for the anthem

Say politicians should stay out of football

I'll leave team selection to the manager. I can't even pick a sock.
One day nobody will ask who sang. They'll only ask who scored.

The next Ivaylo is in a village somewhere right now. Let's give them a gym.

My neighbour's son went to Golba to lay bricks. There are no bricks here to lay.
Let's build a country these three hundred never have to leave again.
{national} lorries held at the Trueant border for eleven days
Its border officers held forty {national} lorries at Crümländ for eleven days, asking for "fees".

Forty {national} lorries have been stuck at the border post outside Crümländ for eleven days. The drivers sleep in their cabs. Trueant officers say the delay will end when certain "processing fees" are paid, in cash.
Close the border to Trueant lorries until ours are free
Every Trueant lorry stays where it is until the last of ours comes home. That's how a border works.
They take our drivers hostage for bribes? Shut the border!
If they won't let our lorries out, theirs can wait with ours. Bring a sandwich.
Send the consul with food and blankets, and keep talking
Food and blankets today, a deal tomorrow. Nobody pays a bribe on our behalf.
First get them a hot meal and a shower. Then argue.
One day that border will be a ten-minute stop. We get there by talking, even now.
Blame the government for letting them push us around
Eleven days! A country that can't get its own drivers home doesn't deserve a foreign ministry!
The minister found time for a holiday this month. Not for forty drivers.
The Trueants test us because they know this government won't answer.
Four {national} aid workers taken hostage in Norbanistan
A militia in northern Norbanistan has seized four volunteers from a Cranebo medical charity. It wants two million Golban dollars. The families are camped outside the foreign ministry.
Say {country} never pays ransom
Pay once, and every {national} abroad becomes a price tag. We bring them home another way.
Not one pezo for gunmen! Find them and bring them back!
If you pay the wolf, he comes back for the rest of the flock.
Bring them home, whatever it costs
They went to save lives. The least their country can do is save theirs.
If it were my daughter, I'd sell the house. They're somebody's daughters.
Four people who went to help strangers. I want to live in the country that brings them home.
Say they knew the risks when they went
Our sympathy is with the families, but the state cannot underwrite every private journey into a war zone.
There's plenty of people to help in Fauran, and nobody gets kidnapped.
Work quietly with the government, and say nothing
A Golban data centre wants {province}'s water

A Golban tech firm plans a huge data centre for its AI models in {province}. It would use as much water as a town of eighty thousand people, during a dry decade. It promises three hundred jobs and a new school.
Welcome it: {country} can't miss the future
Every country is competing for these centres. Turn this one away, and it goes to Dillihan.
Three hundred jobs and a new school. In {province}, that's a lot.
Let {country} be where the future gets built, not where it gets downloaded.
Allow it only if it recycles its water and pays local prices
Build it, but on our terms: recycled water, full price, and the jobs go to local people.
They can have the land. The water, they pay for like the rest of us.
A centre that cools itself and teaches our kids to code. That's a deal worth signing.
Say farms need the water more than computers
In a dry decade, water goes to the people who grow our food. That's not anti-technology, it's arithmetic.
They want our water so a Golban computer can write poems!
You can't eat an algorithm. I checked.
Banks replace six thousand call-centre jobs with AI

The country's three biggest banks will close their call centres in Tarroport by next year and answer customers with AI. Six thousand jobs go, most held by women over forty. Customers say the machine is already more polite.
Tax companies that replace workers with AI
If a machine takes a job, it can pay some of the tax the worker paid.
Six thousand jobs gone so three banks can save on coffee breaks!
I rang my bank last week. The robot was very nice. It still couldn't find my money.
Promise to retrain every one of them
Every worker who loses a job to a machine gets a year's training on full pay.
Nobody in Tarroport is too old to learn. My aunt learned to text at seventy.
These six thousand could be running the machines in five years. Let's pay for that.
Say it's progress and {country} must keep up
The countries that adopt this first will be the rich ones in twenty years.
Machines that answer phones free people to do the work machines can't.
We didn't save the switchboard operators either.
Missing girl found dead near {city}

Mila, eight, went missing on her way home from school in {city} nine days ago. Her body was found this morning in a field outside town. Police have arrested a 41-year-old farmhand. He was born in Norbanistan. The whole country is in mourning.
Visit the family privately, and say nothing in public
Ask why the search took nine days
Her family deserves to know why it took nine days. So does every parent in {country}.
Nine days! The police found a minister's stolen car in nine hours last year!
I don't want a speech from the police chief. I want to know what happened on day one.
Say this is what open borders cost
Norbanian immigrants
How many more children before this government finds out who it let in?
We must ask, calmly, how a man with his past came to be living next to a primary school.
Mila would be alive if our borders were closed. Every one of you knows it.
Call for calm until the trial
A man has been arrested. Let the courts judge him, not the crowd.
Tonight hold your children, and leave the rest to the court.
Influencers turn on you

Barbara Lulli and Jeremy Hannigan, who never talk politics, posted a joint video: "We don't do this, but the things that party says about people are hateful, and our followers should know." Six million views by lunchtime.
Admit you went too far, and soften
Some of what I said was wrong, and the way I said it was worse. I'll do better.
My mother saw the video. Believe me, they're not the hardest critics I've faced today.
I want a country where everyone feels at home, and I haven't always sounded like it. That changes now.
Say rich influencers don't know real life
A gamer and a café blogger lecture working families about hate? Spare us!
I respect their right to their views. I don't need their permission to speak for people they never meet.
Come to Bayernal on a Tuesday, Jeremy. Bring your headphones, it gets loud.
A mural of you appears in {city}

Overnight, artists painted a mural four storeys high on a wall in {city}: you, in a suit, feeding a bonfire with books in every language spoken in {country}. Thousands came to photograph it. Three more appeared by the weekend.
Go and see it, and laugh it off
They got my good side. I didn't know I had one.
Art that makes people argue is doing its job. I've come to look, not to complain.
If they paint me differently in a year, I'll come back and take a photo with that one too.
Demand the city paint over it
That wall is somebody's property. Defacing it is a crime, whatever it shows.
Vandals with paint cans don't get to slander a party of the people!
If I painted my opinion on your house, you'd call the police too.
Say it proves the cultural elite fears you
They paint walls. We knock on doors. Let's see who gets the votes.
Four storeys, all for me. My mother says it's the nicest thing they've ever done.
When the arts world spends this much paint on one party, it tells you who they're afraid of.
A Dillihan drama is the most-watched show in {country}

"The Orchard Wars", a Dillihan family drama about feuding fruit farmers, is the most-watched show in the country. Babies are being named after its characters. Fauran farmers point out that the orchards in it look exactly like theirs.
Say you're watching it too
I'm on season two. Don't tell me what happens to the uncle.
Good stories cross borders. One day the whole region will be watching ours.
It's a fine series. Our neighbours can make good television; so can we.
Fund {national} drama to compete
If Dillihan can make the country's favourite show, so can we, with the right support.
We have feuding farmers too. Ours have better jokes.
The next show the whole region watches should be filmed in Fauran. Let's pay for that.
Call for quotas on foreign television
Half of what's on our screens should be made here. Plenty of countries do it.
Dillihan wants our pastures and our living rooms!
Dillihan patrols take our cattle in the day, and their dramas take our evenings.
Rats in the kitchen that feeds two hundred schools

Inspectors found rat droppings and spoiled meat at the central kitchen that supplies lunches to two hundred schools in Cranbia. It was last inspected four years ago. The number of food inspectors has halved since 2022.
Promise to hire back the inspectors
Every kitchen that feeds children gets inspected every year. That means hiring the inspectors back.
They cut the inspectors to save money and fed the savings to our children!
My kids eat there. I want an inspector in that kitchen more often than the rats.
School lunch should be the best meal some kids eat all day. Let's make it that.
Ban the company and sue its owners
The company loses every public contract it holds, and its owners answer in court.
Lock the doors and put the owners in front of a judge!
If my restaurant served that, I'd be closed by teatime. Same rules for them.
Say parents should pack their children's lunches
Families know best what their children should eat. The state needn't run a kitchen for every school.
My mother packed my lunch for twelve years. Nobody ever found a rat in it.
Cranebo inspectors ban Fauran's raw-milk cheese

New hygiene rules from Cranebo ban the sale of cheese made from raw milk. In Fauran, villages have made it the same way for four hundred years. The cheesemakers have been told to buy stainless steel tanks they can't afford.
Defend the cheesemakers: exempt traditional food
Traditional food made the traditional way deserves its own rules, written with the people who make it.
Four hundred years of cheese, and a clerk in Cranebo knows better!
My grandfather ate that cheese every day and lived to ninety-one. He'd have lived to a hundred if they'd let him.
Let's make Fauran cheese famous across the region instead of illegal at home.
Back the rules: safety comes first
Raw milk can make children seriously ill. Rules for food safety can't depend on where you live.
I like old cheese. I don't like old bacteria.
Offer grants to help them meet the rules
Keep the rules, and pay for the tanks. Safety shouldn't cost a village its living.
If Cranebo wants shiny tanks in Fauran, Cranebo can help buy them.
Same cheese, same villages, cleaner tanks. Fauran can have both.
The river below {city} runs orange

For three days the river below {city} has run orange. Dead fish line the banks for twenty kilometres. A chemical plant upstream admits a "discharge incident". It employs 1,800 people in a town of forty thousand.
Close the plant until it's cleaned up
The plant reopens when it can prove it won't happen again. Not a day before.
They poisoned a river and called it an incident. Shut it down!
My kids used to swim there. Now the fish are floating on their backs.
In five years that river can be clean enough to swim in again. It starts with closing the pipe.
Fine them heavily, but keep the jobs
A fine big enough to hurt, a clean-up they pay for, and eighteen hundred jobs kept.
Make them pay for every fish. And keep the town working.
Make the owners personally pay
The owners live upstream of nothing. Let them pay out of their own pockets!
When a company poisons a river, the people who run it should answer personally, in court.
I'd like to see the chairman's garden pond turn orange. Just for a week.
Calls to ban "Black Harbour" after school knife fights

Two pupils were stabbed in school fights in Tarroport this month. Teachers say boys copy the gang drama "Black Harbour", the country's most-watched series among teenagers. A group of parents wants it banned.
Ban it from television and the apps
Children are copying what they see. Some things don't belong on a screen in every bedroom.
They sell knives to our kids as entertainment! Take it off the air!
When my son started talking like a gangster at breakfast, I knew it had gone too far.
Defend it: banning a show solves nothing
Knife fights existed before television. Banning a series lets us avoid asking why.
They banned a comic when I was a boy. We read it under the bed.
Our kids are smarter than we give them credit for. Talk to them, don't switch them off.
Say boys need somewhere to go, not a ban
A boy with a football club on a Tuesday night isn't watching gang dramas for ideas.
Bored fifteen-year-olds will copy anything. Give them something better to copy.
Every kid in Tarroport with a coach, a team and somewhere to be. That's what beats Black Harbour.
Three women killed by former partners in one week

Three women were killed by former partners this week, in Cranebo, Nikecisa and Kansilia. All three had gone to the police. Two had restraining orders. Thousands marched in silence last night; the question now is who failed them.
Blame the police: they were warned and did nothing
Three women asked the police for help. Every one of those reports must be investigated, and someone must answer.
They went to the police and were sent home! How many warnings does it take?
My sister reported a man once. The officer asked what she'd done to upset him.
A woman who goes to the police should walk out safer than she walked in. We can build that.
Blame soft courts: tougher sentences
A restraining order means nothing if breaking it costs nothing. Breaking one should mean prison.
Two of them had court orders! The courts gave those men a piece of paper and a second chance!
A restraining order is a sheet of paper. Paper never stopped anybody.
Blame a culture that treats women as property
This doesn't start with a knife. It starts with jokes, with silence, with 'it's a family matter'.
Men who think they own women are made, not born. Ask who made them!
Our daughters can grow up in a country where this is unthinkable. It's up to us, all of us.
Listen to the four-hour podcasts our sons are listening to, and you'll understand this week.
Blame men from abroad
Ask where these men came from, and who let them in!
We must ask whether some of the men coming to {country} share our values about women.
Interior minister asked who looks after her children

On live television, the interviewer asked Interior Minister Claire Anderson, in the middle of a border crisis, who looks after her two children while she works such long hours. Nobody has ever asked her male colleagues. The clip is everywhere.
Call the question out
Ask her about the border. That's her job, and it's the question the country needs answered.
In twenty years nobody has asked a male minister who minds his kids. Not once!
I've been asked about my party, my money and my tie. Never about who's feeding my children.
One day that question will sound as strange as asking her if she can read. Let's get there quickly.
Say it's a fair question for any parent
Every parent in public life should be asked how they balance it. Fathers too.
My mother would have asked her the same thing. Then she'd have offered to babysit.
Stay out of it: you'd rather talk about the border
I'll leave the interviewers to argue among themselves. The border is the story.
Mario Goranov: women are "too emotional for a crisis"

On his four-hour podcast, Mario Goranov told a million listeners, most of them young men, that women in government are "too emotional to lead in a crisis". He has invited every party leader on his show next week. Two have already said yes.
Condemn it, and refuse his invitation
Half the people who kept this country running through every crisis were women. I won't sit next to someone who says otherwise.
My grandmother ran a farm through a drought and a war. Mr Goranov can tell her about emotions.
Our daughters should grow up thinking that's a strange thing to say. I'd like to help with that.
Go on the show anyway: his listeners vote too
I'll go where the voters are. I won't agree with everything said in the studio.
A million young men listen to him. Somebody should talk to them about rent.
I'll go on, as long as nobody gets too emotional about it.
Petition to ban hunting reaches 400,000 signatures
An animal welfare group from Cranebo has gathered 400,000 signatures for a national ban on hunting with dogs and shooting deer for sport. In Erland and Fauran, the season opens next week.
Back the ban
Killing animals for sport has no place in a modern country. Farmers who need to control pests keep every right they need.
Twenty dogs after one fox isn't tradition, it's cruelty!
I've never understood how you can love the countryside and spend Sunday shooting it.
One day our grandchildren will see deer in every forest and wonder why anyone shot them.
Defend the hunt
Hunting keeps the deer in balance and the villages alive. People who've never lived there shouldn't write its rules.
Cranebo wants to ban everything it doesn't understand!
My grandfather hunted, my father hunted. The deer are still there, and so are we.
Half the people who signed think venison grows in plastic trays.
Ban hunting with dogs, keep licensed shooting
Ban the cruelty, keep the licence. Most hunters already do it that way.
No dogs, a proper licence, and everybody's home for lunch.
One in six young men has gambling debts

Every shirt in the top football league carries a betting company's name. A new study finds one in six young men in {country} owes money on bets. A bill would ban betting adverts at matches and on television.
Ban the adverts
No betting adverts before the evening news, and none on a shirt a child wears.
They hook boys on betting before they can shave!
My nephew lost his rent on a corner kick. A corner kick.
Let football be a game our kids love again, not a betting slip.
Leave adults to make their own choices
Adults decide what to do with their own money. Help the ones who struggle; don't ban the rest.
If we banned every advert for something bad for you, the breaks would be very short.
Tax the betting firms to pay for addiction help
A levy on every bet, and every pezo of it for people who can't stop.
If they make money on the losses, they can pay for the help.
Let the people who got rich on this pay for a way out of it.
Facial-recognition cameras for every square in Cranebo

After a bomb scare on the metro, the interior ministry wants facial-recognition cameras in every station and square in Cranebo. It says wanted criminals would be found in seconds. It won't say who else would be.
Back the cameras
If a camera finds a wanted man before he boards a train, it has done its job.
Criminals hide in crowds. Let's take the crowd away from them!
My face is in a hundred photos from my cousin's wedding. One more won't hurt.
A metro where nobody thinks twice about the last train home. The cameras can buy that.
A country that tracks every face is a country where nobody dares protest.
Today it's wanted criminals. Tomorrow it's everyone who marched last Saturday!
I'd like to buy bread without the ministry knowing which loaf.
Let's be a country safe enough that it doesn't need to watch everyone.
Allow them only with a judge's warrant
Cameras that switch on only with a judge's warrant, for a named suspect. Nothing else.
Fine, but a judge holds the key, not the minister.
Cranebo's police chief had eight million pezos in James
Cranebo's police chief kept a private account in James holding eight million pezos. Officers now say promotions in his force were sold for cash.
Demand an outside review of the whole force
Every promotion he signed should be reviewed by people from outside the force.
If the man at the top was for sale, who else was?
My cousin waited eleven years to make sergeant. Now we know why.
Most officers are honest. Let's give them a force they can be proud of again.
Defend the officers: one bad apple
One corrupt chief doesn't make a corrupt force. Prosecute him and let the rest work.
Twenty thousand officers didn't buy their stripes. Don't punish them for one man.
Blame the government that appointed him
The interior minister picked him personally! Who picked the minister?
The government hired him, praised him and gave him a medal last spring.
If you want to know how this government chooses people, look at its police chief.
MPs vote themselves a 30% pay rise
Parliament voted itself a 30% pay rise at eleven o'clock last night, by a show of hands. Teachers got 3% this year.
Promise your MPs will take only what teachers got
Our MPs will take the same rise as teachers: three percent.
Thirty percent, at eleven at night, while the country slept!
If I gave myself thirty percent, my family would ask who I'd robbed.
Imagine a parliament that only gets a raise when the country does.
Tie MPs' pay to the average wage
From now on, MPs' pay moves with the average wage. Up or down.
If the country does well, they do well. That's how it works for everyone else.
Defend it: pay MPs well or only the rich will stand
Pay MPs badly, and only the rich and the corrupt will want the job.
Pay peanuts and you get monkeys. Then again, look around parliament.
Government to sell the state railway
To cut the debt, the government plans to sell the state railway to a consortium led by a Golban investment fund. Fares would be "set by the market". Rural lines would be "reviewed".
Oppose the sale
Railways are roads with rails. We don't sell the roads.
They want to sell the trains our grandparents paid for to a fund in Golba!
"Reviewed" means the train to my village stops coming.
Trains to every town, on time, owned by the people who ride them. We can fix it without selling it.
Support the sale
The state has run the railway into the ground for thirty years. Someone else should try.
New owners, new trains and a timetable you can trust. Let's give it a chance.
Have you been on the Kravk train? Selling it is an act of mercy.
Sell it only to {national} buyers
If it's sold, it's sold to {national} owners, with the rural lines guaranteed by law.
Not one sleeper of our railway to a Golban fund!
A nuclear power plant near {city}
The government proposes {country}'s first nuclear power plant, on the coast near {city}, built by Potanian engineers. Electricity bills would fall by a fifth within ten years.
Back the plant
Cheap, steady power for fifty years. Most serious countries did this long ago.
My electricity bill is bigger than my food bill. I'll take the power station.
Power cheap enough that the factories come back. That's what this plant can mean.
Oppose it: too risky
We have sun, wind and a sea. We don't need to leave our grandchildren a problem buried on the coast.
A reactor next to {city}, and Potania holds the keys!
Nobody wants a reactor at the end of the garden. Including the minister, who lives in Cranebo.
Let's be the country that runs on its own sun and sea.
Back it, but built by {national} firms
Build it, with {national} engineers and {national} steel.
If we're having a reactor, I'd like to know the man who welded it.
CraneCoin collapses; pensioners lose their savings

CraneCoin, a digital currency advertised on every Clipr feed for a year, collapsed overnight. Its founder has left for James. Forty thousand {nationals}, many of them pensioners, have lost their savings.
Compensate the victims
Pensioners who lost their savings to a fraud the state failed to stop deserve help from the state.
My neighbour put his whole pension in. He thought it was a bank.
Nobody who worked forty years should end up broke because of an advert on a phone. Let's make them whole.
Regulate it like a bank, and ban the adverts
Anyone selling investments to the public follows the same rules as a bank. No exceptions.
Where were the regulators while CraneCoin was on every phone in the country?
Say people must take responsibility
Nobody was forced to buy it. The state can't insure every bad investment.
If something promises to double your money in a week, it's doubling somebody's money.
Demand James hand over the founder
James is our friend. A friend hands over a thief.
Bring him back from James in handcuffs!
Births fall to a record low; the NUP offers 40,000 pezos a child
Births in {country} have fallen to the lowest since records began. The NUP proposes paying 40,000 pezos for every child born.
Back the bonus
A country that stops having children has decided to grow old. Forty thousand pezos is a start.
My parents raised four of us on one wage. Today two children take two wages and a grandmother.
Let's be a country where young people want to start a family, and can afford to.
Say homes and childcare matter more than cash
Nobody has a child for forty thousand pezos. They have one when they have a home and childcare.
Forty thousand pezos buys a pram. It doesn't buy a second bedroom.
Give young couples a home, a nursery and a decent wage, and the children will come.
Say immigration can fill the gap
Every country with fewer births welcomes workers. We should choose ours well.
If we won't have the children, someone else's will run our hospitals.
Say it's a couple's choice, not the state's
Whether to have children is nobody's business but the couple's.
My aunt never had children, and she's the happiest person I know.
A nursery place now costs more than rent
A nursery place in Cranebo now costs more than the average rent. One in four parents who stopped working after a child says childcare is the reason.
Promise free childcare from age one
Free childcare from the first birthday. It pays for itself in parents who can work.
Working families are paying a second rent just to go to work!
My sister did the sums. She was paying to go to her job.
Every parent free to work, every child in a good nursery. Other countries do it; so can we.
Cut taxes for families instead
Let families keep more of what they earn, and choose their own care.
I'd rather have the money and pick the nursery myself.
Pay parents who stay home instead
Pay a parent who stays home with the children what we'd pay a nursery.
The best nursery I ever saw was my grandmother's kitchen.
Two kilometres of tents along Cranebo's river
Tents line the river in Cranebo for two kilometres. The city counts four thousand people sleeping rough, twice as many as three years ago. Shopkeepers want them moved.
Promise a home first, then everything else
A door that locks comes first. Then the job, the treatment and the rest.
Four thousand people in tents in the capital of a rich country. Shame!
Most of them had a flat two years ago. The rent did this.
Every one of those tents could be a front door within a year. We know how to do it.
Clear the camps and offer shelter beds
Nobody has the right to camp on a public riverbank. Offer every one of them a bed, and clear the tents.
Shopkeepers can't open their doors! Enough!
Cranebo used to have a river. Now it has a campsite.
Say most of them aren't {nationals}
Count how many of those tents were here before the boats came!
We must ask why our shelters are full of people who arrived last year.
University fees of 16,000 pezos a year
The government wants to charge university students 16,000 pezos a year. Until now, university has been free. Students have occupied the main hall of Cranebo University.
Keep university free
Free university gave this country its doctors and engineers. Don't charge the next ones.
They studied for free, and now they want your children to pay!
I was the first in my family to go. At sixteen thousand a year, I wouldn't have.
Every bright kid in Fauran should be able to study in Cranebo. Let's keep it that way.
Back fees, with grants for poorer students
Graduates earn more. It's fair they pay something back, with grants for those who can't.
A plumber's taxes pay for a lawyer's degree. That never seemed right to me.
Say too many people go to university
We need more electricians and fewer graduates driving taxis. Fund apprenticeships.
My plumber earns more than my lawyer, and he answers the phone.
Half these degrees are a three-year holiday on the taxpayer.
The last doctor in {province}'s valleys retires
The last doctor in {province}'s eastern valleys retired this month. Thirty villages now share one ambulance, which takes ninety minutes to arrive.
Pay doctors more to work in the countryside
Double pay and a free house for doctors who work in rural valleys. It has worked everywhere it's been tried.
Nobody falls ill on a timetable. A village needs a doctor, not a bus to one.
A doctor in every valley again. It's not much to ask, and we can do it in five years.
Make new doctors serve three years in the countryside
The state pays for medical school. Three years in a village is a fair thing to ask back.
Plenty of us did military service somewhere we'd never heard of. Three years in Fauran won't hurt them.
A clinic on wheels and doctors by video
A clinic on wheels every week, and a doctor on a screen in every village hall.
The best doctors in Cranebo, in every village, the same afternoon. The technology is already here.
Golba offers a defence pact, and wants a base
Golba offers {country} a defence pact: Golban protection if any neighbour attacks, in return for a Golban air base near {city} and an order for Golban fighter jets.
With the Trueants claiming Alinni and Bordon rearming, a guarantee from Golba is worth a base.
If you live on a rough street, you make friends with the biggest family on it.
With Golba beside us, our children grow up without fearing the next border crisis.
Refuse: no foreign troops on {national} soil
{country} defends itself. Our soil isn't rented to anyone's air force.
A Golban base, Golban jets and Golban orders? We are not a colony!
Once a guest moves in with his jets, he doesn't move out.
Let's be strong enough not to need anyone's base.
Say {country} should stay neutral
Neutral countries are rarely invaded and always invited. Let's be one.
The quiet neighbour is the one nobody fights with.
Let {country} be where this region's quarrels get settled, not started.
Government cuts foreign aid by two thirds
The government will cut foreign aid by two thirds, including a programme of clinics in Norbanistan. "Charity begins at home," says the finance minister.
Back the cut
Every pezo spent abroad is a pezo not spent in Fauran. Our own people come first.
Clinics in Norbanistan while Fauran's villages have none!
You fix your own roof before you fix the neighbour's.
Defend the aid budget
A clinic in Norbanistan costs less than a refugee ship in Nikecisa.
When we had the earthquake, half the region sent help. Neighbours remember.
Let {country} be known as the country that helps. It costs less than people think.
Keep the money, but spend it on Fauran's clinics
Keep the budget, and send every pezo of it to Fauran's clinics.
Let's build in Fauran what we were building abroad. Then, one day, both.
Wildfires across {province} in a record heatwave
Wildfires are burning across {province} in the worst heatwave on record. Eleven villages have been evacuated. Firefighters say half their trucks are older than they are.
Go there and help
I came to listen to the firefighters, not to make speeches.
I brought water and a shovel. I'm told I'm better with the water.
Fauran will grow back greener than before, and we'll help it.
Demand new fire trucks and planes
Every province gets the planes and trucks it needs before next summer. Not after the next fire.
Our firefighters are fighting this with trucks from the last century!
My uncle's tractor is newer than his village's fire truck.
Say the climate is changing and we must plan for it
Summers like this will be normal by 2040. We should plan for them now: forests, water, firebreaks.
How many villages have to burn before Cranebo takes this seriously?
We can still choose what kind of summers our children have. Let's start choosing.
Blame arsonists and demand harsh sentences
Most wildfires are started by people. Every one of them must face the full weight of the law.
Somebody lit these fires. Find them and lock them up for life!
New schoolbooks call 1964 a "reunification"
